title: On Uniform Error Bounds for Kernel Regression under Non-Gaussian Noise
claim: The posterior variance is overly conservative with little data, while the proposed kernel- and data-dependent terms stay tighter and converge as data accumulates.
layout: 3 panels in a row (t=4, 10, more), shared legend on top, data ticks below
description: A horizontal strip of line plots sharing one legend at the top. The legend shows black × marks for input data x_1..x_t, a solid blue line for the posterior variance σ_t²(x), a green dash-dotted line for ρ²‖h_t(x)‖₂², and an orange dotted line for ρ²‖h_t(x)‖_∞². Each panel has a different number of observations t (t=4, t=10, and a larger t cut off at the right edge). The x-axis runs from 0 to 10 with grey gridlines, and × markers along the bottom show where data lies. At t=4 the blue curve stays high between and beyond the data points while the green and orange curves sit lower and dip sharply at the right. By t=10 the curves come closer together. In the third panel, with many data points, blue and green nearly coincide and orange sits below them. The eye goes first to the blue curve, then to how the gap to the other curves changes across panels.

abstract: Providing non-conservative uncertainty quantification for function estimates derived from noisy observations remains a fundamental challenge in statistical machine learning, particularly for applications in safety-critical domains. In this work, we propose novel non-asymptotic probabilistic uniform error bounds for kernel-based regression. Compared to related bounds in the literature that are restricted to (conditionally) independent sub-Gaussian noise, our bounds allow to consider a broad class of non-Gaussian distributions, such as sub-Gaussian, bounded, sub-exponential, and variance/moment-bounded noise. Moreover, our results apply to correlated and uncorrelated noise. We compare our proposed error bounds with existing results in terms of the induced uncertainty region and their performance in safe control, demonstrating the tightness of the proposed bounds.
